webservice_origins.description: Allowed origins for cross-origin WebSocket connections. Add every public URL through which Cockpit is reached (e.g. 'https://cockpit.example.com'). Leave empty when not using a reverse proxy.

webservice_protocol_header.description: HTTP request header that your reverse proxy sets to indicate whether the client is using HTTPS. Typically 'X-Forwarded-Proto'. Leave empty when Cockpit handles TLS directly.

webservice_login_title.description: Title text displayed on the Cockpit login page. Customise to identify the environment (e.g. company name or datacenter).

webservice_compression.description: Enable gzip compression for HTTP responses. Reduces bandwidth for slow links; disable if a reverse proxy handles compression upstream.

webservice_max_startups.description: Maximum number of concurrent unauthenticated connection attempts cockpit-ws will accept. Excess connections are refused until slots free up.

webservice_allow_multihost.description: Allow users to connect to additional remote hosts from the Cockpit UI. Enable only if the host-switching feature is needed and access is controlled at the network layer.

webservice_client_cert_auth.description: Require a TLS client certificate for authentication. Only effective when cockpit-ws terminates TLS itself (not behind a proxy). Requires a PKI to issue client certificates.

session_idle_timeout.description: Minutes of browser inactivity before the session is automatically closed. Set to 0 to keep sessions alive indefinitely (not recommended for shared systems).

session_banner.description: Absolute path to a plain-text file displayed on the login page before users authenticate (e.g. a legal notice or acceptable-use policy). Leave empty to show no banner.

log_fatal_channels.description: Cockpit bridge log channels treated as fatal — cockpit-ws exits when an error is emitted on any listed channel. 'stderr' covers the most critical bridge errors; add 'auth' to make authentication errors fatal.
